findings.title: `sed -i ''` only works with BSD/macOS sed and fails on Linux.
findings.body: GNU sed does not accept the separate empty-string backup argument. It reads `''` as the script and the real expression as a file name, so on Linux the command fails and `GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL` is never replaced. The script then still prints "✅ Updated GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL". Fix: use a portable form, such as `sed -i.bak -E ... && rm "$ENV_FILE.bak"`, or write to a temp file and move it into place.

findings.title: `updateMany` with empty data probably never bumps `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt`.
findings.body: The comment says this updates `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt` for every calendar under the credential, but the call passes `{}` as the data. When Prisma gets no fields to set, it skips the write, and `@updatedAt` only fills in when a real update happens. So after a webhook refresh the timestamp most likely stays the same, and anything that reads `updatedAt` to show freshness gets a stale value. I could not check the exact Prisma version's behaviour from here. Fix: set the field explicitly.

findings.title: Cache timestamp is always formatted in `en-US`, whatever the user's locale.
findings.body: The "Last updated" string is translated, but the date inside it is always formatted with `"en-US"`. Users with another locale see US month/day ordering and a 12-hour clock, which is confusing in places like the EU, where 07/08 means August 7th. Fix: take the locale from `useLocale()` (`i18n.language`) and pass it to `Intl.DateTimeFormat`.

held.title: The hand-edited DEFAULT NOW() may not match schema.prisma and cause migration drift.
held.body: The generated migration was edited by hand to add `DEFAULT NOW()`. If the `CalendarCache.updatedAt` field in `schema.prisma` is declared as `DateTime @updatedAt` without `@default(now())`, the database and the schema no longer agree. The next `prisma migrate dev` will report drift and generate an unrelated `ALTER COLUMN "updatedAt" DROP DEFAULT` migration, or ask to reset the dev database. I could not see the schema.prisma hunk to confirm this. Fix: declare the field as `updatedAt DateTime @default(now()) @updatedAt` so the schema matches this SQL. Separately, every existing cache row will report the migration time as its `cacheUpdatedAt` until it is next written, so the new UI will show stale caches as freshly updated.
